subject: EU routing: analytics vendor onboarding & subprocessor notification
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@dataflux.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@dataflux.io
Date: 2026-10-05 08:12 +0100
Subject: Question about SignalWave subprocessor and EU routing

Hannah —

Thanks for the heads-up in the roadmap email yesterday. Our legal and security teams reviewed the note that Redwood plans to onboard SignalWave Analytics as an analytics subprocessor. Before we proceed with the pilot, can you confirm the following: 

- The scope: what data categories will SignalWave process? (telemetry, anonymized usage metrics, raw prompts, embeddings?)
- Data residency: will any DataFlux customer data (or derived artifacts) leave EU regions?
- Retention: proposed retention period for logs and aggregated analytics
- Controls: is there an executed subprocessor agreement / DPA annex and evidence of SignalWave's security controls (SOC2 or equivalent)?

We'd appreciate a short dataflow diagram and the subprocessor questionnaire/annex. We have an internal procurement cutoff next week, so a response by EOD 6 Oct would be ideal.

Best,
Nora
Nora Patel
Senior Legal Counsel — Data & Privacy
DataFlux

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@dataflux.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, SignalWave Ops <ops@signalwave-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 11:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about SignalWave subprocessor and EU routing

Nora —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: SignalWave is being onboarded as a telemetry/usage analytics provider only — they will not receive raw customer prompts or model training data. All DataFlux customer identifiers are hashed before routing to SignalWave. We are attaching the dataflow map and the signed DPA annex for SignalWave.

Attachments: dataflow-map-signalwave.pdf (dataflow diagram), dpa-annex-signalwave-signed.pdf (signed DPA annex, limited subprocessor scope)

Answers to your bullets:
- Scope: telemetry and aggregated usage metrics (latency, feature flags, anonymized event counts). No full prompt payloads are sent.
- Data residency: SignalWave instances that will process DataFlux telemetry are hosted in the EU (Frankfurt and Amsterdam regions). Redwood routing will pin DataFlux traffic to EU hosts.
- Retention: analytics events retained 30 days by default; aggregated summaries kept 12 months. We can adjust retention shorter by contract.
- Controls: SignalWave has completed our security review and provided SOC 2 Type II (attestation) and encryption-at-rest keys managed in EU KMS. The signed subprocessor annex is attached.

Next steps: Lauren (legal) and Marcus (infra) are cc'd to confirm operational details and provide the internal evidence link. If anything in the annex is insufficient for your procurement, please flag the exact clause and we’ll escalate.

Regards,

Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@dataflux.io>
Date: 2026-10-05 14:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about SignalWave subprocessor and EU routing

Hannah / Nora —

Confirming the operational details from infra: 
- Deployment: SignalWave tenant instances for DataFlux are deployed to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and eu-west-1 (Amsterdam). No failover routing will cross to us-east unless explicitly authorized; cross-region failover requires a documented incident and customer opt-in.
- Data sent: only anonymized telemetry summary events and aggregated metrics. We strip message bodies and truncate identifiers before forwarding.
- Retention/config: default 30-day event retention, aggregated metrics 12 months. We can implement a contractually-required 7/30-day retention window for specific accounts (config flag: retention_profile=dataflux_short).
- Logs/audit: access logs for SignalWave processing are retained in our EU observability store for 30 days; we can provide filtered access logs on request for compliance reviews.

Internal reference: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/infra/signalwave-deploy (internal evidence and runbook)

Attachment (internal): signalwave-config-notes.txt

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Nora —

Thanks for the questions. For procurement/legal clarity: 
- We have a signed subprocessor annex with SignalWave attached (dpa-annex-signalwave-signed.pdf). The annex includes EU SCCs (where applicable) and standard liability/processing clauses aligned to our master DPA.
- Security evidence: SignalWave provided a current SOC 2 Type II report and an internal security questionnaire (hosted in the Drive link below). We have a signed Data Processing Addendum and a separate Subprocessor Agreement; I have inserted those into the shared drive for your review.
- If your procurement requires any contractual changes (e.g., deletion SLA, stricter logging access), please list the specific clauses you want changed. For most customers we can offer a targeted retention SLA and audit access under an addendum.

Shared evidence: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/security/signalwave-review

Action items: 
1) Nora — confirm whether a 30-day event retention is acceptable or if you need the 7/30 profile;
2) Redwood (Lauren) — upon confirmation, we will provide a short acceptance email + signed annex for procurement.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop

lauren_bishop@redwood.com
